scenes.text: This is Cedar — an autonomous yield agent on the Casper network. Since our last update, it does something most agents only claim to: it moves real capital, under a mandate it can prove it obeyed. Here's what's new.

First — you set the strategy in plain English. Tell Cedar: stay conservative, and keep at least twenty percent in the stable pool. A language model — Llama three point three — reads that mandate and decides. But the model doesn't get the last word. A deterministic engine re-derives the move and checks it against your mandate's safety envelope. Cap a move at twenty percent, and even if the model wants to move five hundred, it's held to two hundred. The AI proposes. The rules dispose.

Second — and this is the big one — Cedar now custodies real CSPR. The vault is an Odra smart contract that actually holds the funds. Deposits and withdrawals are real on-chain transfers. And an on-chain invariant guarantees every allocation is backed, one to one, by real value inside the contract. This is not a ledger of intent — it's real capital. Deposit, reallocate, withdraw: every one verifiable on the explorer.

Every move still clears the same safety pipeline. Observe live yields and the on-chain balance. Validate — bad data is rejected before the model ever sees it. Reason, then recheck. Guardrails: cooldown, position cap, cost versus gain. Then, and only then, actuate — sign, and submit to Casper. No confirm button. No human in the loop.

And it refuses. Every figure the model cites is checked against real data — fabricate a number, and the cycle is force-held, in code, not a prompt. Every decision, and every refusal, is logged with the exact reason it fired.

It's live right now, at try cedar dot x-y-z — governing a real four hundred and sixty-five CSPR position on testnet. The dashboard streams every cycle: the mandate, the reasoning in plain English, the reallocations with their transaction hashes, and the moves it blocked.
Cedar. Real capital. Plain-English mandates. Provable obedience. Open source, MIT licensed, live on Casper testnet — for the Casper Agentic Buildathon.
